correctness.rationale: The definition uses the Euclidean distance between F and the convex hull of all vertices absent from F, rather than a supporting-hyperplane margin. Each proper face is a signed one-per-axis subset I. For |I|<d, a missing axis puts 0 in the complementary hull, and every complementary vertex has nonpositive signed coordinates along I; minimizing ||(a_i alpha_i)|| with sum alpha=1 yields 1/sqrt(sum_I a_i^-2), attained by alpha_i proportional a_i^-2. For facets complement=-F, convexity implies min ||x+z||=2 min_F||x||=2/sqrt(sum_all a_i^-2). Strict enlargement of I and the facet/nonfacet inequality show minimizers are exactly (d-1)-faces omitting an axis of maximal a_i, with 2^(d-1) sign choices for each such axis. Diameter 2 max a_i and normalized rigidity follow directly. I checked the inequalities at d=2 and tie cases and independently solved convex-pair quadratic programs for representative d=2,3,4 weights: 114 pairs in this run and further source checker face enumerations; largest residual of the independent QP run was under 5e-14. Finite QPs are corroboration, not proof of arbitrary d.
residual_risks: Finite numerical or exhaustive small-parameter checks do not prove unbounded cases; only the reconstructed analytic argument supports universal claims.
